title: Emergency department triage
goal: Show a safe emergency-department triage process with acuity-based disposition.

rubric.must: An immediate-life-threat decision visibly routes Yes to a resuscitation bay and stabilisation.
The diagram visibly has separate terminators for admission-or-transfer and discharge-with-advice.
High-acuity symptoms visibly route to urgent clinician assessment while lower acuity enters standard assessment.
Failure to meet discharge criteria visibly leads to observation and reassessment back toward clinical testing.
A minor-treatment eligibility decision visibly separates minor treatment from urgent assessment.
Yes and No labels make the triage decisions visually legible.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the flowchart exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The target shows the requested triage paths and both distinct dispositions. Decision branches are labeled and traceable; the observation loop returns toward testing. No material overlap or cropping is visible.

items.evidence: “Immediate life threat?” routes Yes left to “Resuscitation bay,” then down to “Stabilise and investigate.”
Separate end terminators are labeled “Admit or transfer” and “Discharge with advice.”
“High-acuity symptoms?” routes Yes to “Urgent clinician assessment” and No to “Standard assessment queue.”
“Discharge criteria met?” routes No to “Observe and reassess”; a dashed loop returns toward “Tests and treatment.”
“Safe for minor-treatment stream?” routes Yes to “Minor treatment” and No back toward “Urgent clinician assessment.”
Yes and No labels are visibly placed at the decision branches; the routing is traceable.
